name: Centor/McIsaac Criteria

citations.text: McIsaac WJ, White D, Tannenbaum D, Low DE. A clinical score to reduce unnecessary antibiotic use in patients with sore throat. CMAJ. 1998;158(1):75-83.
Centor RM, Witherspoon JM, Dalton HP, Brody CE, Link K. The diagnosis of strep throat in adults in the emergency room. Med Decis Making. 1981;1(3):239-246.

validated_population: Children age 3 and older and adults with a sore throat seen in primary care (McIsaac); adults in the emergency room (Centor, 1981).
self_report_note: The original studies used findings recorded by a clinician. Swollen glands and throat patches are harder to judge yourself.
license_note: Published clinical decision rule; criteria are not a copyrighted instrument. Question wording is original to OLA BOT.

red_flags.question: Are you unable to swallow your own saliva, or are you drooling because it hurts too much to swallow?
red_flags.help: Answer yes if you are spitting out saliva instead of swallowing it.

red_flags.question: Is there a high-pitched or noisy sound when breathing in, or a muffled "hot potato" voice?
red_flags.help: A harsh, whistling sound when breathing in can mean the airway is narrowing.

red_flags.question: Is one side of your throat much worse, with trouble opening your mouth fully?
red_flags.help: This pattern can mean a pocket of pus near the tonsil, which needs an exam today.

items.question: How old is the person with the sore throat?
items.help: The chance of strep throat is highest in school-age children and lower after age 45.

items.question: Have you had a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher?
items.help: Count a fever measured with a thermometer during this illness. If you did not measure, choose Not sure.

items.question: Is your cough absent? (Answer yes if you do NOT have a cough.)
items.help: A cough makes a cold virus more likely than strep. Answer yes if you have no cough at all.

items.question: Are the glands on the front of your neck, just under the jaw, swollen or sore to the touch?
items.help: Press gently on both sides of the neck just below the angle of the jaw. Answer yes if there are tender lumps.

items.question: Are your tonsils swollen, or do you see white patches on them?
items.help: Use a flashlight and a mirror. Tonsils are at the back of the throat on both sides. Answer yes for swelling or white or yellow spots.

scoring.threshold_text: −1 to 1 = low likelihood; 2 to 3 = moderate likelihood; 4 to 5 = high likelihood of strep

overrides.label: Age under 3 (outside the validated age range)

low.label: Low likelihood of strep
low.interpretation: About 1 to 10 in 100 people with this score have strep throat. A virus is the most likely cause.
low.recommendation: No strep test or antibiotics needed. Treat symptoms at home.

care.within: Manage at home; see primary care if not better in 5 to 7 days
care.where_detail: Home care. Book a primary care visit if the sore throat lasts more than 7 days or you get worse.
self_care: Acetaminophen or ibuprofen as labeled for pain and fever.
Warm salt-water gargles or throat lozenges.

moderate.label: Moderate likelihood of strep
moderate.interpretation: About 11 to 35 in 100 people with this score have strep throat.
moderate.recommendation: Rapid strep test or throat culture advised. Antibiotics only if the test is positive.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic with an on-site rapid strep test, or a primary care visit within 24 hours.
ed_redirect: Severe throat pain with trouble swallowing liquids

high.label: High likelihood of strep
high.interpretation: About 50 in 100 people with this score have strep throat.
high.recommendation: Rapid strep test or throat culture advised today. Antibiotics if the test is positive.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic with an on-site rapid strep test.
ed_redirect: Severe throat pain with trouble swallowing liquids

not_applicable.label: Rule does not apply (child under 3)
not_applicable.interpretation: The McIsaac score was not validated in children under 3. Strep throat is uncommon at this age, but other infections need an exam.
not_applicable.recommendation: Have a pediatric clinician examine the child.

care.where_detail: Pediatric or family medicine clinic, or urgent care that sees young children.
ed_redirect: Fever in a baby under 3 months
Not drinking or fewer wet diapers
Hard to wake or breathing fast
